how: npm run fuzz: fast-check properties (src/fuzz/properties.ts) at high run counts, each within a time limit, with a fixed seed per property; a failure is shrunk to a small counterexample and kept with the seed and path that replay it. In process, no network.
canonicalization: Terms are canonicalized with RFC 8785 (JCS): keys sorted by UTF-16 code units, no whitespace, strings escaped as JSON.stringify escapes them (lone surrogates as \uXXXX). Key order and the whitespace the JSON was written with never change the hash (terms-order-whitespace).

No Unicode normalization is done anywhere: a payee written in NFC (é, U+00E9) and in NFD (e + U+0301) are different code points, so different canonical bytes and different hashes (terms-unicode). The passkey signs the exact code points the phone shows and hashes itself; a normalized copy of the terms would be refused, never accepted.

Terms carry no JSON numbers: money is a two-decimal string. The runner (src/lib/terms.ts), the receipt verifier (src/try/receipt.ts) and /verify (src/proof/bundle.ts) refuse a number anywhere in the terms (terms-numbers). The phone's canonicalize (src/approve/client.ts) would write a finite number in JS form; it never meets one, since the terms it hashes come from the runner. /verify's JCS writes whole numbers only, for the ledger entries a bundle carries.

Amounts are compared as strings: 1850.00, 1850.0, 1,850.00 and "1850.00 " are four different terms with four different hashes (terms-numbers). The reader turns what a document says into dddd.dd before anything is proposed (parser-total).

The four implementations (the runner's metal-pay jcs, the phone's, the receipt verifier's and /verify's) write the same bytes for any number-free JSON, and Node's SHA-256 and WebCrypto's agree (terms-four-canonicals-agree).

results.target: parseApFallback (src/ap/reading.ts), the reader /try uses offline and every fallback uses
results.what: on any text (invoice lines, random unicode, binary, 100-5,000 repeats of what its regexes look for) it never throws, answers in under 2 s, reads a total only as dddd.dd, an IBAN and an invoice number only as written in the text (an IBAN failing mod 97 is read as written, for the checker to block: iban_invalid)

results.what: every invoice checkCompose accepts, written in the sample's layout, is read back by the parser with the same number, total, IBAN and due date

results.target: the same through the PDF /try renders (src/engine/invoicePdf.ts) and the text extraction (src/ap/pdfText.ts)
results.what: every invoice checkCompose accepts, rendered to the enterprise PDF and its text extracted, is read back with the same number, total, IBAN and due date

results.target: parseInvoiceFallback (src/claude/invoiceReading.ts), the runner's invoice reader without a model
results.what: on any text it either reads an invoice whose amount is dddd.dd and whose IBAN and number are written in the text, or refuses with its own error ("invoice: ..."); never another exception

results.target: termsHash (src/lib/terms.ts): the hash a passkey signs
results.what: any change of any field (a character, a key renamed, removed or added, a type swapped, a value replaced) either makes the terms unhashable (refused) or changes the hash
the hash is the same whatever the key order (at every depth) and whatever whitespace the JSON was written with

results.target: the four canonical forms: the runner's (src/lib/terms.ts, metal-pay jcs), the phone's (src/approve/client.ts), the receipt verifier's (src/try/receipt.ts) and /verify's (src/proof/bundle.ts)
results.what: on any number-free JSON (lone surrogates, unicode keys, __proto__ included) all four write the same bytes, and Node's SHA-256 and the phone's WebCrypto SHA-256 agree

canonicalization does no Unicode normalization: a payee written in NFC and the same text in NFD (different code points) hash differently, and the canonical text gives back exactly the code points it was given

results.target: canonicalTerms and the verifiers: numbers and number formats
results.what: a JSON number anywhere in the terms is refused by the runner, the receipt verifier and /verify (money is a decimal string); amounts written differently (1850.00, 1850.0, 1,850.00, 1850.00 with a space) are different strings and never share a hash

results.target: verifyProofBundle (src/proof/bundle.ts: /verify and npm run verify-bundle), on the committed bundles
results.what: a change to anything the passkey's signature covers (the terms and their hash, the canonical text, rp_id, origin, the assertion, the public key) is never VALID

results.target: verifyProofBundle: the context a bundle carries beside the signature (the engine's decision, the ledger entries of the payment and the ledger's head)
results.what: the decision the engine recorded and the ledger entries /verify shows as "ledger balance" and "ledger chain" cannot be changed or dropped without a check failing

results.target: verifyReceipt (src/try/receipt.ts: /try/verify and npm run verify-receipt), on the committed receipts
results.what: a change to anything the signature covers (the terms and their hash, rp_id, origin, the assertion, the public key) is never valid, and any input at all is answered without throwing

results.target: hookSignatureOk (src/policy/cardHooks.ts): the runner's check of Airwallex's x-signature
results.what: the true HMAC-SHA256(secret, x-timestamp + body) verifies (in either hex case); a one-character change to the timestamp, the body or the signature, another secret, or any other string never does; nothing throws

results.target: receiveAccountEvent and receivePartnerEvent (cloud/src/awxPlatform.ts, cloud/src/connect.ts): Purser Cloud's Airwallex webhooks
results.what: any request whose x-signature is not HMAC-SHA256(secret, x-timestamp + body) or whose x-timestamp is not within 5 minutes is refused with 401, before anything is read or written; nothing else is ever thrown

results.target: Purser Cloud's MCP server (cloud/src/claude/mcp.ts mcpAnswer): every tool, any JSON-RPC message
results.what: any message is answered without throwing (no 5xx); a tool call is carried out only when its arguments fit the tool's own published inputSchema (checked here with Ajv); nothing approves, pays or writes

results.target: the agent API's MCP server (src/platform/mcpServer.ts): every tool an outside agent can call
results.what: any arguments to any tool are refused or handled: a call that succeeds fits the tool's published inputSchema (Ajv), nothing is approved, no card is issued or charged, the policy is never changed
